findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests" and "employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date"
findings.fix: Specify whether physical receipts are required or if photos are acceptable - for example, change to "employees shall retain receipts (as photos or originals) for one year after the purchase date."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether retaining a photo satisfies the one-year retention requirement or if physical receipts must be kept.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break into multiple shorter sentences that separately explain the conditions for approval, the requirements that must be met, and how the device is tracked against budget.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence is too long with multiple interconnected clauses, making the second-device policy requirement difficult to understand.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form," "you submit the request in the portal," and "You track its status" versus "employees" or "the employee" used throughout other sections
findings.fix: Rewrite using consistent third person - replace "You record" with "The employee records," "you submit" with "The employee submits," and "You track" with "The employee tracks."
findings.violation: This section uses second person ("you") while the rest of the policy uses third person, creating inconsistency in voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either add the remaining steps in the process or remove "begins with" if these are the only required steps.
findings.violation: The phrase "begins with" implies additional steps follow, but no other steps are listed, making the section appear incomplete.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time" appears identically in both Program Overview and Special Cases; Special Cases says "finance liaison reviews the stipend budget" while Program Overview says "benefits team tracks the stipend budget"
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence and clarify which department - benefits team or finance liaison - is responsible for reviewing the stipend budget.
findings.violation: The section duplicates a sentence from Program Overview and introduces a conflicting department for budget responsibility.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year" in Questions and Updates contradicts "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year" in Program Overview
findings.fix: Consolidate all budget-tracking responsibilities into the Program Overview section and explicitly clarify which department owns each task, or explain if multiple departments share overlapping roles.
findings.violation: Three different departments are mentioned throughout the document as tracking or reviewing the budget, with no explanation of their distinct responsibilities.
